description: Recognition-tier items: a felt situation, four candidate verses, one that speaks most directly. Deliberately a SEPARATE table from bible-verses.js. These are relational items (a set of 4 + a judgement), not properties of a single verse, so they cannot be derived from per-verse Category tags.
designRules: Scope the question to a concrete scenario, never an abstract need. "Which helps most with anxiety?" has several defensible answers and is therefore unfair.

Every wrong option must be ruled out by a FACT the scenario states, quoted verbatim in "ruleOut". A player must be able to eliminate it with certainty, not by taste. "Less helpful" is not a reason; "does not apply" is.
No near-misses. A distractor that a reasonable person might still pick is a bad distractor, even if the answer is defensible on reflection.
The strongest rule-out is a contradiction: the verse tells you to do what the scenario says you have already done, or assumes something the scenario says you lack.
The answer carries a "cue": a verbatim fragment of the scenario that it answers. If no deciding detail can be quoted, the scenario is too vague.
Every option carries a "topic" (2-4 words). Topics must be distinct, and no distractor topic may be cued by the scenario text.
The need word may appear in at most one option, so the item cannot be solved by scanning for a word.
Tier 1 of the difficulty ladder. Never gate progress behind recall modes before the player has won something.
